source: NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2; weights per DoD Assessment Methodology v1.2.1

controls.title: Authorized Access Control
controls.plain: Only let approved people, devices, and programs into systems that hold sensitive defense data.

controls.title: Transaction & Function Control
controls.plain: Limit each user to the kinds of actions and transactions their job actually requires.

controls.title: CUI Flow Enforcement
controls.plain: Control where sensitive defense data is allowed to travel, following rules you have set.

controls.title: Separation of Duties
controls.plain: Split key job duties among different people so no one person can misuse the systems alone.

controls.title: Least Privilege
controls.plain: Give each person only the minimum access their job needs, including for administrator accounts and security tools.

controls.title: Non-Privileged Account Use
controls.plain: Require administrators to use a separate, everyday account when they are not doing administrator work.

controls.title: Privileged Functions
controls.plain: Stop ordinary users from running administrator functions, and record each time someone runs one.

controls.title: Unsuccessful Login Attempts
controls.plain: Lock accounts or slow down sign-in after too many wrong password attempts.

controls.title: Privacy & Security Notices
controls.plain: Show a sign-in notice that states the privacy and security rules that apply to your sensitive defense data.

controls.title: Session Lock
controls.plain: Lock the screen after a period of inactivity, and hide what was on it.

controls.title: Session Termination
controls.plain: Automatically end user sessions after a set period of inactivity.

controls.title: Remote Access Control
controls.plain: Monitor and control remote access to your systems.

controls.title: Remote Access Confidentiality
controls.plain: Use encryption to protect remote access sessions so outsiders cannot read the traffic.

controls.title: Remote Access Routing
controls.plain: Send all remote access through a small number of managed, secured access points.

controls.title: Privileged Remote Access
controls.plain: Approve in advance any remote administrator commands and any remote access to security settings and logs.

controls.title: Wireless Access Authorization
controls.plain: Approve wireless access before anyone connects to your network over Wi-Fi.

controls.title: Wireless Authentication & Encryption
controls.plain: Protect wireless networks by checking who connects and encrypting the traffic.

controls.title: Mobile Device Connection
controls.plain: Control the connection of mobile devices, such as phones and tablets.

controls.title: Encrypt CUI on Mobile
controls.plain: Encrypt sensitive defense data stored on phones, tablets, and other mobile devices.

controls.title: External Connections
controls.plain: Check and limit any connection to, or use of, outside systems such as personal devices and cloud services.

controls.title: Portable Storage
controls.plain: Limit when staff may plug company USB drives and similar portable storage into outside computers.

controls.title: Public Information
controls.plain: Control sensitive defense data posted or processed on publicly accessible systems, which anyone can reach.

controls.title: Role-Based Risk Awareness
controls.plain: Make sure managers, system administrators, and users know the security risks of their work and the security rules that apply.

controls.title: Role-Based Training
controls.plain: Train staff to carry out their security duties, with training matched to each role.

controls.title: Insider Threat Awareness
controls.plain: Teach staff to recognize and report warning signs of insider threats.

controls.title: System Auditing
controls.plain: Keep records of system activity so you can find, study, and report unlawful or unauthorized actions.

controls.title: User Accountability
controls.plain: Record enough detail in your logs to trace each action back to the person who did it.

controls.title: Event Review
controls.plain: Review, on a set schedule, which events your systems log, and update that list when needs change.

controls.title: Audit Failure Alerting
controls.plain: Send an alert when logging stops working.

controls.title: Audit Correlation
controls.plain: Link audit record review, analysis, and reporting so they work together to investigate and respond to unlawful, unauthorized, suspicious, or unusual activity.

controls.title: Reduction & Reporting
controls.plain: Provide tools that sort and summarize logs so reviews and reports are quick.

controls.title: Authoritative Time Source
controls.plain: Set all system clocks from a trusted time source so log timestamps match.

controls.title: Audit Protection
controls.plain: Protect log records and logging tools from unauthorized access, changes, and deletion.

controls.title: Audit Management
controls.plain: Let only a few trusted administrators manage your logging tools.

controls.title: System Baselining
controls.plain: Create and maintain standard setups and inventories of your systems, including hardware, software, firmware, and documents, through each system's life cycle.

controls.title: Security Configuration Enforcement
controls.plain: Set and enforce security settings for the technology products your systems use, such as computers, routers, printers, and software.

controls.title: System Change Management
controls.plain: Track, review, approve or reject, and log changes to your systems.

controls.title: Security Impact Analysis
controls.plain: Check how a planned change could affect security before you make it.

controls.title: Access Restrictions for Change
controls.plain: Write down and approve who may change your systems, physically or through software, and enforce those limits.

controls.title: Least Functionality
controls.plain: Set systems to run only the features and services people truly need.

controls.title: Nonessential Functionality
controls.plain: Restrict, turn off, or block the use of programs, functions, ports (network doors), protocols, and services you do not need.

controls.title: Application Execution Policy
controls.plain: Use a block list of banned software, or an allow list of approved programs that blocks everything else.

controls.title: User-Installed Software
controls.plain: Control and monitor software that users install themselves.

controls.title: Identify System Users
controls.plain: Give every user, process, and device its own identity so you know who is who.

controls.title: Authenticate Users
controls.plain: Verify the identity of each user, process, or device before it gets access to your systems.

controls.title: Multifactor Authentication
controls.plain: Require a second sign-in step, like a phone code, for all network sign-ins and for every administrator sign-in, including local ones.

controls.title: Replay-Resistant Auth
controls.plain: Use sign-in methods that cannot be recorded and replayed, for network access to admin and regular user accounts.

controls.title: Identifier Management
controls.plain: Do not reuse identifiers for people, groups, roles, or devices for a set period after they are retired.

controls.title: Identifier Handling
controls.plain: Turn off user identifiers after a set period of inactivity.

controls.title: Password Complexity
controls.plain: Require a minimum password length and mix of characters, and require new passwords to differ from old ones by several characters.

controls.title: Password Reuse
controls.plain: Block people from reusing a password for a set number of password changes.

controls.title: Temporary Passwords
controls.plain: Make temporary passwords work only once, and require a new password at first sign-in.

controls.title: Cryptographic Key-Based Auth
controls.plain: Store and send only scrambled versions of passwords, never the passwords themselves.

controls.title: Obscure Authentication Feedback
controls.plain: Hide typed passwords on screen so people nearby cannot read them.

controls.title: Incident Handling
controls.plain: Set up a working way to handle security incidents: prepare, detect, analyze, contain, recover, and help affected users.

controls.title: Incident Reporting
controls.plain: Track and document security incidents, and report them to the right people inside and outside the company.

controls.title: Incident Response Testing
controls.plain: Test your incident response plan to see whether it works.

controls.title: Perform Maintenance
controls.plain: Keep your systems maintained and in good working order.

controls.title: System Maintenance Control
controls.plain: Control the tools, methods, and people that perform maintenance on your systems.

controls.title: Equipment Sanitization
controls.plain: Wipe sensitive defense data from equipment so it cannot be recovered before sending it off-site for maintenance or repair.

controls.title: Media Inspection
controls.plain: Scan maintenance diagnostic and test media for harmful programs before using it on your systems.

controls.title: Nonlocal Maintenance
controls.plain: Require a second sign-in step, like a phone code, for remote maintenance, and end the connection when the work is done.

controls.title: Maintenance Personnel
controls.plain: Supervise maintenance staff who do not already have approved access.

controls.title: Media Protection
controls.plain: Protect paper and digital media that hold sensitive defense data, and store it securely.

controls.title: Media Access
controls.plain: Let only authorized people use media that holds sensitive defense data.

controls.title: Media Sanitization
controls.plain: Wipe or destroy media that held sensitive defense data before you throw it away or reuse it.

controls.title: Media Marking
controls.plain: Mark media, such as drives and paper, with the needed sensitive defense data markings and limits on sharing.

controls.title: Media Accountability
controls.plain: Control media that holds sensitive defense data, and keep track of it whenever it leaves secured areas.

controls.title: Portable Storage Encryption
controls.plain: Encrypt sensitive defense data on drives and media you transport, unless physical safeguards like a locked case protect them.

controls.title: Removable Media
controls.plain: Control the use of removable media, such as USB drives, on company systems.

controls.title: Shared Media
controls.plain: Ban portable storage devices that have no known owner.

controls.title: Protect Backups
controls.plain: Protect the confidentiality of backup copies that hold sensitive defense data.

controls.title: Screen Individuals
controls.plain: Screen people before you give them access to systems that hold sensitive defense data.

controls.title: Personnel Actions
controls.plain: Protect sensitive defense data when people leave or move jobs, including removing their access promptly.

controls.title: Limit Physical Access
controls.plain: Limit physical access to your systems, equipment, and work areas to authorized people.

controls.title: Monitor Facility
controls.plain: Protect and monitor your building and the power, cooling, and wiring that keep your systems running.

controls.title: Escort Visitors
controls.plain: Escort visitors and watch what they do while they are in your facility.

controls.title: Physical Access Logs
controls.plain: Keep audit logs of physical access, such as a sign-in sheet or badge records.

controls.title: Manage Physical Access
controls.plain: Control keys, badges, and other physical access devices, and keep track of who has them.

controls.title: Alternative Work Sites
controls.plain: Enforce safeguards for sensitive defense data at alternate work sites, such as home offices.

controls.title: Risk Assessments
controls.plain: Regularly assess risks to your operations, assets, and people from running your systems and handling sensitive defense data on them.

controls.title: Vulnerability Scan
controls.plain: Scan your systems and applications for weaknesses on a schedule, and whenever new weaknesses affecting them are announced.

controls.title: Vulnerability Remediation
controls.plain: Fix vulnerabilities, meaning security weaknesses, in line with your risk assessments.

controls.title: Security Control Assessment
controls.plain: Check your security controls on a regular schedule to confirm they work.

controls.title: Plan of Action
controls.plain: Write and carry out plans of action designed to correct gaps and reduce or eliminate weaknesses in your systems.

controls.title: Security Control Monitoring
controls.plain: Keep watching your security controls over time to be sure they keep working.

controls.title: System Security Plan
controls.plain: Write, and regularly update, security plans describing your systems’ boundaries, operating environments, connections to other systems, and how each requirement is met.

controls.title: Boundary Protection
controls.plain: Monitor, control, and protect the information your systems send or receive at the external boundaries and key internal boundaries.

controls.title: Architectural Design
controls.plain: Build security into how you design your systems and write software, rather than adding it afterward.

controls.title: Role Separation
controls.plain: Keep user functions separate from system management functions.

controls.title: Shared Resource Control
controls.plain: Stop information from leaking between users who share the same system resources.

controls.title: Public-Access System Separation
controls.plain: Place public-facing systems on separate networks from your internal systems.

controls.title: Network Communication by Exception
controls.plain: Block all network traffic by default, and allow only the traffic you have approved.

controls.title: Split Tunneling
controls.plain: Stop remote devices from connecting to your network and to outside networks at the same time.

controls.title: CUI in Transit
controls.plain: Encrypt sensitive defense data while it travels over networks, unless physical safeguards protect the connection.

controls.title: Network Disconnect
controls.plain: End network connections after a set period of inactivity, or when the session ends.

controls.title: Key Management
controls.plain: Set up and manage the keys used for encryption.

controls.title: CUI Encryption
controls.plain: Whenever you encrypt sensitive defense data, use encryption modules the government has tested and certified, called FIPS-validated.

controls.title: Collaborative Device Control
controls.plain: Block remote turning on of cameras and microphones, and tell users when they are in use.

controls.title: Mobile Code
controls.plain: Set rules for, and monitor, code that downloads and runs in browsers or email.

controls.title: Voice-over-IP
controls.plain: Set rules for, and monitor, internet phone calls (VoIP).

controls.title: Communications Authenticity
controls.plain: Protect network sessions so each side can trust who it is connected to and that the session is not hijacked or faked.

controls.title: Data at Rest
controls.plain: Protect sensitive defense data while it is stored, such as on disks and in cloud storage.

controls.title: Flaw Remediation
controls.plain: Find, report, and fix flaws in your systems in a timely manner.

controls.title: Malicious Code Protection
controls.plain: Protect your systems from viruses and other harmful programs at the places where they can enter.

controls.title: Security Alerts & Advisories
controls.plain: Watch for security alerts and advisories, and act on them.

controls.title: Update Malicious Code Protection
controls.plain: Keep your anti-virus and malicious code protection up to date as new releases come out.

controls.title: System & File Scanning
controls.plain: Scan your systems regularly, and scan files from outside sources as they are opened or downloaded.

controls.title: Monitor Inbound Communications
controls.plain: Watch your systems and network traffic, coming in and going out, for attacks and signs of trouble.

controls.title: Identify Unauthorized Use
controls.plain: Identify any use of your systems that is not authorized.
